physicalNotes: Radius 0.32563175 Jupiter radii from Kendall et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.547f2189K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547f2189K/abstract): 23,280.1 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.06009532 Jupiter masses (Kendall et al. 2026, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2026MNRAS.547f2189K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.547f2189K/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. sources.period: Kendall et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.547f2189K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KENDALL_ET_AL_2026): P 43.12655 d
sources.shape: Kendall et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.547f2189K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KENDALL_ET_AL_2026): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 0.257 au and stellar radius 1.367 solar radii; Kendall et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.547f2189K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KENDALL_ET_AL_2026): inclination 88.874 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Kendall et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.547f2189K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KENDALL_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2459282.7925 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 8 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
